## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sīlavattheragāthā* (Thag 12.1) is a poem located in the *Theragāthā* of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. The verses extol the supreme value and pervasive benefits of ethical conduct (*sīla*), describing virtue as bringing every manner of success (*sabbasampattiṃ upanāmeti*) [Keown 1992]. According to Damien Keown, the text and its commentary highlight a threefold happiness produced by morality—a good reputation, worldly goods, and rebirth in heaven or final nibbāna—while observing that the moral person (*sīlavā*) wins many friends [Keown 1992].

SuttaCentral notes curated passage-level parallels in the *Itivuttaka* (*Sukhapatthanā Sutta*, Iti 76) and in the Chinese Buddhist canon at T 765.124 [SuttaCentral]. In addition, DharmaNexus identifies machine-computed cross-language text reuse with Tibetan texts, finding alignments with the *Śīlaparikathā* (D4164) across six segments (e.g., §4.2 aligning with §169a-34–169a-35) and with the *Śrāvakabhūmi* in the *Yogācārabhūmi* (D4036) across four segments (e.g., §2.3 aligning with §24b-21) [DharmaNexus]. An English translation of the verses has been produced by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].
